definition: A neural network with many layers between input and output — depth enables hierarchical feature learning behind modern AI.
details: A neural network with many layers between input and output — depth enables hierarchical feature learning behind modern AI.

explainer.lead: A deep neural network is a neural network with many processing layers between its input and its output. Those layers can build features step by step, allowing later layers to work with increasingly high-level patterns.

tiers.eli5: Imagine passing a picture through a team of helpers, where each helper notices something and passes their notes to the next. Early helpers might notice simple marks, while later ones combine those notes into more useful clues. A deep neural network works like this team, with many layers helping it turn an input into an answer.
tiers.practitioner: A practitioner feeds numerical inputs through a stack of hidden layers and reads the result from the output layer. The central architectural choice is how to organize that depth so the network can learn hierarchical features; adding layers also changes the computation required.
tiers.paperLevel: A DNN can be expressed as f(x) = f_L(...f_2(f_1(x))...), where f_1 through f_L are successive layers and the hidden layers between input and output provide depth. Composing many layers lets the network represent hierarchical features rather than relying only on a single transformation of the input.

explainer.example: For an image-classification task, the input layer receives the image's pixel values, successive hidden layers transform them into increasingly useful features, and the output layer produces the network's predicted category.

usedIn.name: Image recognition
usedIn.detail: Layered features can help turn pixel inputs into category predictions.

usedIn.name: Speech recognition
usedIn.detail: Deep networks can process audio-derived inputs to support recognition tasks.

usedIn.name: Language processing
usedIn.detail: Many-layer networks can learn features used in modern language systems.

components.name: Input layer
components.detail: Receives the numerical representation of the data.

components.name: Hidden layers
components.detail: Apply successive transformations that build hierarchical features.

components.name: Output layer
components.detail: Produces the network's final result for the task.

flow: Data is encoded as numbers and passed to the input layer.
The first hidden layer transforms those values into features.
Later hidden layers combine earlier features into higher-level features.
The output layer turns the final representation into a result.
explainer.whyItMatters: Depth gives neural networks a way to learn features at multiple levels instead of requiring every useful feature to be supplied directly. This hierarchical feature learning is a key part of modern AI.
